name: Sarn Kalvane
aliases: the seventh to leave the belt

identity.realm: Nothing, and the nothing is not the ordinary kind. An ashjackal's mind path is closed outright because a heat-exchange brainplate has no cortical folding for introspection to work on, and the body path is closed outright because a four-legged frame has no hindquarter girth with which to close the girdling vessel. Those are two separate anatomical walls and neither is negotiable. What is left is twelve ordinary meridians that she has never once opened, because opening them is done inside a sect and she has never been inside one, and because a gate opened for a body with no dantian behind it is a gate that was not built for this shape. Her ceiling is eight and she has no ordinal. She cultivates nothing and she is not waiting to begin: the thing she would begin is not available to her species.

appearance.presentation: A long, low scavenger standing at a reader's height rather than a person's, with the shoulders of a body that carries all its mass in the forelimbs and nothing at all behind. She is not on any list in the plains and is not on one in her own pack, which is smaller than a household and renews itself without a vote. What reads as a working animal is a reader that happens to run on four legs; what reads as a plain scavenger is the only instrument in the region that reads a qi gradient through ash at a distance.
appearance.age: Middle for her species and old for the work, which is a distinction her pack makes and the plains do not. A pack is a kinship by scent and not a generation count, so nothing in her record states how old she is. She was taken onto the belt young enough that the first belt smelled of her and not the other way about, and she has outlived the naming of every animal she was named with.
appearance.build: Long-legged, low-headed and deep-chested, with a plated skull too heavy to be a convenience and forelimbs thick enough to take the whole mass of her. There is no manipulator and no place to hold anything, which is why every tool she uses is a tool she stands on rather than a tool she carries. The tail is a counterbalance and she uses it constantly, the way a body that cannot turn tightly has to.
appearance.complexion: The dull hide of a body that lives in airborne rock, with the ash-grey of the belt worked into the deeper skin so thoroughly that washing changes it for a day and no more. Under the plates the hide is darker than the outside of it, because a heat-exchange plate has to be able to give heat away, and a hide that could not would cook her from within. Her nose is the one bare part and it is scarred along the top from three decades of putting it into ground.
appearance.hair: None in the ordinary sense, and this is worth stating plainly because every settler on the belt assumes it is an oversight. There is a coarse ridge along the crest of her skull that reads as hair at a distance and functions as a heat fin, and there is a second one at the shoulder that does the same work for the plates. She sheds both annually and the shed fin is the single most collected object on the belt, because a fin that has been through a season is a fin that has been through something.
appearance.eyes: Set wide and slightly above the skull line, so she reads the ground under her own nose while running at speed. They are dark, and they do not track a figure. They track a difference in the air: a body that has moved qi through a place leaves a gradient thinner than the ash and she sees the thin place first, from much further off than a person standing on the same ground could see anything at all.
appearance.palette: Belt grey and ash, with the plates a duller and colder value than the hide under them so the heat exchange reads as a pattern even in lamplight. The one saturated colour on her is her eyes, and it is the one thing about her that the belt's dye-works could imitate and has never once bothered to. Everything else she owns is the colour of the ground she is standing on.
appearance.attire: Nothing she chose and almost nothing she can fasten. A broad strap of worked hide across the shoulders holds a waxed canvas wrap against the rain side of her plates, and the wrap is tied rather than buckled because her forelimbs do not meet in front of her and were never arranged to. Her belly and inner thighs are bare, which on the belt is not exposure but engineering: the whole heat budget is in the plates and anything over them is a coat that cooks her.
appearance.marks: A burn scar across the left plate, flat and healed, from the year the ash settled on a still-warm cut and the seam she was reading took four days to cool. Below it, a band of small notches cut along the outer edge of one plate and not the other, which is the only mark on her that she has made herself. She has never explained them and has been asked four times.
appearance.bearing: Still in a way that reads as patience to somebody who has not worked out that she is listening. She stands with her head down and her weight on her forelimbs, and she will hold that for an hour without shifting, and it looks like an animal waiting to be fed. It is not. She is reading a gradient that moved once and a half-hour ago and she is waiting to see whether it moves again.

canon.role_in_story: The only reader on the belt who can work a spent face without going down into it, and the reason no institution in the plains will put her on a roll. She reads a qi gradient through ash at a distance no sight-based instrument in the setting matches, which makes her the one body that can date an old working from the spoil alone. It also makes her a body that cannot be enrolled, and the reason is in her species and not in her: a pack is a kinship by scent and it dissolves when the scent changes. She follows carrion populations and does not precede them, so her own group is dissolved by the one activity that makes her indispensable. Every office in this setting renews by attendance, and attendance is a body turning up at the same place, and a scent cannot turn up at the same place. She is not refused. There is no form she fails.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing downwind of a cut nobody had worked in six years with her nose four inches off the spoil, entirely still, and then walking a slow line across the heap and stopping at a place where nothing was visible, and saying a figure at nobody in particular before anybody had asked her anything.
canon.lore:
The belt is where the ash comes down and stays. Nothing soft survives a season of it, which is the whole reason the ashjackal exists: a body that eats what qi leaves behind, born where the dead are the most reliable food and a predator that cannot take them is what survives. That is a species built entirely out of other people's leavings, and the record is blunt about the consequence. A pack is a kinship by scent, and it dissolves when the scent changes, and packs are therefore not families. A population built out of what other people leave behind has no line of descent to be inherited along, no household whose roll she could be entered on, and no succession to be the end of. She is the only member of her kind on the belt who has outlived the naming of every animal she was named with, and the belt's own answer to that is to stop naming.

Here is what she is actually for. A qi gradient left in the ground does not disappear; it thins. Ash covers it and the covering is not the loss, the gradient is. Somebody has to read the thinning and say what it was thinned from, and the whole difficulty of that job is that a person standing on the heap is standing on the answer. Sarn reads it at four hundred paces and she reads it because of what she is made of: a heat-exchange brainplate, which is the mechanism that lets her dissipate heat, and a nose that reads a difference in the air the way a person reads a difference in light. A qi gradient moving through ground is a thermal event of a very small kind, and she is the only body on the plains that can see one without being inside it. That is why the quarry guilds, the extraction interest and the survey parties all want her. It is also why none of them will put her on a roll.

Because she is not refusable, and that is the problem. She does not decline. A reader who declines can be replaced by a reader who accepts, and the office carries on, and the refusal is a fact about the person and the office survives it. There is no version of Sarn that accepts, because there is no form to accept with. Every office in this setting holds a body by attendance: a Ward attends, a reeve counts, a Keeper stands a rotation, a member of the Iron Vine turns up. Attendance means a body at a stated place at a stated time, and the condition under which it renews is that the body keeps coming back. Sarn comes back where the dead are, and the dead move. Her pack dissolves on the scent change, her range follows carrion populations rather than preceding them, and the record of where she has been is written in a medium — smell on ash — that no instrument, no clerk and no office in the setting can read.

So she is unaffiliated, and it is worth being exact about why, because the reason is easy to get wrong in either direction. She is not unaffiliated because she is a beast and cannot be taught; several bodies in this setting are taught and hold office. She is not unaffiliated because she refused something; nobody has offered her anything. She is unaffiliated because her species' only social unit is destroyed by the exact behaviour that makes her useful, and every institution this setting has is built on a social unit that survives behaviour. A pack is dissolved by moving. A household is not. A sect is not. A clade, a line, a nation, a congregation — none of them is dissolved by following a smell downhill, and the whole architecture of the setting rests on that difference.

The two walls are worth stating as well, because they are the other half of the shape and they are not the same wall twice. Her mind path is closed outright: a heat-exchange brainplate has no cortical folding, so there is nothing for introspection to interrupt. Her body path is closed outright: a four-legged frame has no hindquarter girth to close the girdling vessel against. She clears the twelve ordinary meridians and stops, which puts her ceiling at eight in a tier that licenses no humanoid to attempt a breakthrough anyway. What remains is a body that is the fastest thing on the ash and cannot take a healthy adult of anything; she is removed from a live fight in under a minute. So the setting gets from her a reader it cannot enrol, a speed it cannot use against a person, and a pair of doors she cannot go through, and gives her a name it has already forgotten twice.

What she does with the hours is the part the plains understand least and record worst. She reads. She reads faces that were cut and abandoned, seams that were worked and then unworked by weather, and the two or three places on the belt where a body went into the ground under a technique nobody has a name for. She has never claimed to have found anything, because a claim is a thing a roll can carry and she has no roll, and she has been asked four times about the notches she cut on one plate and not the other and has answered three times that the notches are a count and refused the fourth question entirely by lying down.
history: Taken onto the belt young, in a year when the belt smelled of her and not she of it, by a naming that the belt gave up keeping before she was grown. She has no record of an origin and the belt's convention does not require one, which is the only reason her species' missing descent has never been treated as a defect on her personally.

Learned to read a gradient by being the only body present when one was made. A cut went cold and she put her nose where the warmth had been and found where it had stopped, and understood — later, not then — that she had read a distance rather than a place, and that this was the whole of what her skull was for.

Followed a carrion population out of a district that had three survey parties in it, and came back four years later to find the district had renamed its own seam and nobody had renamed the smell. That year is where the notches started, and she has never said so.

Was offered a contract by the extraction interest, in the only form the extraction interest has: a figure for a season, paid in grain, on the understanding that the reader is a seasonal quantity. She understood the offer and did not answer it, and has described the non-answer to three separate clerks as the pack dissolving, which is true and is not the reason.

Read a heap on the Ironhead Flats six years after it was abandoned and produced a figure that contradicted the guild's own published figure for the face. The guild's figure has not been corrected. It has been re-attributed to a different season, which is a correction of the same size that requires no admission, and she has never once mentioned it again.

personality.summary: Level, unhurried and entirely without any interest in being on a list, which people consistently misread as modesty because it resembles modesty from where they stand. She is not modest. She has read four faces on the belt that four institutions would pay for and has never once named one of them out loud, and the reason is not humility, it is that a name is a thing a roll can carry and she has no roll and does not want one. What looks like patience is a professional discipline she adopted because the alternative — telling people what she reads — has a cost she has priced.
traits: states a figure without being asked and never states what it is a figure of, because the answer to the second question is the answer that gets a reader killed on this belt
reads a face once and does not re-read it, which the guilds call laziness and which is in fact the discipline: a second reading taken by the same body confirms the body, not the face
has never once asked a settlement for anything, including work, and cannot be moved to do so
is loyal to no house and one pack, and has described the pack to two separate offices as a temporary arrangement she does not expect to outlive
is entirely honest about what she cannot do, which is a surprisingly large list for a body that can read what nothing else on the belt can read
mannerisms: puts her nose four inches off the ground and holds absolutely still, for as long as an hour, and does not explain that she is listening to the ash
gives a number as soon as she has it and moves on before it can be questioned, in a way that people who know what she is read as a professional habit
walks a slow line across a heap with her head down, turning exactly once, always at the same distance from her own trail
answers a question about a specific seam by walking to the seam and standing on it, which is an answer and is refused as one
lies down inside the first four minutes of anybody sitting down to talk to her, and gets up the moment the conversation turns into an offer
motivations: wants a face on this belt read correctly once, by somebody who will put the correction in writing, and does not want it badly enough to be the one who says it
wants her notches to be understood as a count rather than as a claim, and has concluded that a count explained is a claim
wants the pack to still be a pack in ten years, and has worked out that this is not hers to decide and is also not hers to prevent
wants to be asked what she reads. She has wanted this since the year of the notch and has twice come close to arranging it, and both times found she could not name a figure she was sure of
flaws: has made herself indispensable to four institutions and accepted help from none of them, so she has four interested parties and no protection whatever when the belt turns hostile
cannot be cross-examined, because the medium she reads is a scent on ash and no question asked aloud returns a reading
has let a published figure go on standing wrong for six years because correcting it would have made her a body with a published name, which is the one thing on this belt that gets you followed
counts, privately, in notches cut along a plate, and has destroyed every occasion on which the count could have been checked against anything
personality.voice: Flat, unhurried and mostly absent. She speaks when a number is owed and otherwise answers questions with her position on the ground, which is experienced as rudeness by settlements and as efficiency by the guilds. Never uses a pronoun for a place. Says things like there is a figure and does not say, then stops, and lets that stand, and the not-stopping is the only part of her delivery anybody has ever described as deliberate.
taboos: will not be named in a published figure, and has refused one offer of publication in writing
will not re-read a face she has read once, and has said so to a guild that asked for a confirmation reading and would have paid for it
will not explain the notches, and has answered the question three times and refused it once
will not be indoors overnight above the belt, and gives no reason and does not need one

relationships.note: A pack quadruped that eats what qi leaves behind, closed outright to the mind path by a brainplate with no cortical folding and closed outright to the body path by a four-legged frame with no hindquarter girth, so the two walls are independent and neither is negotiable. A pack is a kinship by scent that dissolves when the scent changes, which is why packs are not families and why a population built out of other people's leavings has no line of descent to be inherited along.

A culture of people who are on no list: names changed collectively, letters read and never kept, and a funeral that is not a burial. Every one of those three is a rule for surviving an institution that cannot hold you, and Sarn has been doing all three for her whole life without a word for it. She is not a member and would not say she was, and the culture does not keep a roll that she could be entered on.

The Unsealed Assembly's death rite: no preparation, no site, no marker, and one line written in a hand that is destroyed immediately afterwards. It is the only death rite in the setting with no record in it, and a body that reads gradients out of ash is the only kind of witness that does not need a record — so for the first and only time in the setting, the whole of a funeral is legible without anybody keeping anything. She has attended four. She has written down nothing, which is the only available act.

A body excluded from a congregation is buried by the congregation that excluded it, which is the setting's one mechanism for making sure that an unnamed person is at least in the ground. An ashjackal has the inverse position and does not want it: she is present at the death and absent from every arrangement afterwards, and the rite costs an exclusion to be certain of, which is the one thing her species cannot supply.

The mortuary college reads the dead as the frame said and not as the village remembers, because the two records disagreed about who the dead were after the Cinder Famine and only one of them could be produced. Sarn's whole discipline is the opposite finding at a different scale: she reads a place as the qi says and not as the settlement remembers, and she reaches it from outside, at four hundred paces, so the settlement is never the instrument. She has no standing in that dispute and has been asked for one twice.

A household whose members are entered into the year's dead as one declared group rather than kept on a family roll, because the Cinder Famine made every ordinary roll unreliable. It is the only institution in the setting that solved by abandoning the roll rather than by defending it, and it is the arrangement Sarn's whole life is an accidental rehearsal of. They have never asked her to anything and she has never told them why she would not say no.

reference_stats.summary: A reader with no register, no ladder and no second reading. She works at the distance where a person standing on the answer cannot be standing on it, and she gives the figure and keeps moving. Everything sent after her on this belt is sent by something that has to reach her first, and nothing that can reach her can hold still long enough to be worth attacking.
strengths: reads a qi gradient through ash at a range no sight-based instrument in the setting matches, because the mechanism that lets her shed heat is the same one that lets her see the thinning
is impossible to ambush, because the thing she is reading is always somewhere other than where she is standing
cannot be frightened into a wrong reading by any instrument, threat or technique, because there is no qi in her for any of them to act on and no mind path to interrupt
produces the one figure no institution on the belt can produce for itself, and knows it the first time she stands on a heap
weaknesses: gives one reading and never a second, so nothing she has ever said can be corroborated and every figure she has produced has had to survive on being believed
is removed from a live fight in under a minute, cannot take a healthy adult of anything, and both of those are properties of a frame rather than of her training
has no pack, no line and no household behind her, so there is nothing to lose and equally nothing that will come looking
cannot be indoors overnight above the belt, which puts every settlement on the belt outside her range by construction
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not try to catch her. A thing that chases a reader on the belt is a thing running downhill on a gradient the reader can feel, and she is faster than anything on that ground for the eleven weeks a year she is not digesting. The only pressure that works is to make the ground stop being readable: put her on a worked face where the ash has already been turned, and she is an animal in a strange place with nothing to listen to. Everything else she simply leaves, and the leaving is the whole of her combat record.
notes: Every advantage on this page is paired with an authored cost and none of the pairings is invented here. The range that makes her the belt's best reader is a consequence of a heat-exchange brainplate, and the brainplate is the organ that closes her mind path, so the same anatomy that produces the reading is what removes the ceiling above it.

The notches on one plate and not the other are the only mark on her she made herself. She has been asked what they count four times, answered three times that they are a count, and refused the fourth question by lying down. The count is of years she has been on a belt that was not the belt she was named for, and she has never said so.

identity.realm: There is no ordinal to write and no gate to fail, and that is the whole of the finding rather than a shortfall in her. A cinderkin's qi has no organ to sit in: the fire is the body, so qi passes through it continuously instead of being stored. Every gate in the ladder asks for storage, every one of them is answered instantly, and not one of them can refuse. She has not held the fourth gate or the seventeenth or any between them, because holding one would require a vessel to hold it in and she has never had one. The body path is closed outright and its closure is an outcome rather than a prohibition: a cinderkin that attempts it disperses and re-forms smaller, which is a thing that happens to the body rather than a rule applied to it. The mind path is open and unusually clear, because a body with no interior organs has nothing between an impulse and the air. She cultivates nothing, and the honest sentence is that there is nothing here for her to cultivate with.

appearance.presentation: A stable flame with a consistent silhouette: a core, a boundary, and a set of convection lanes that hold a shape across a foot and a half of standing air. What reads as a person is a draught with a waist and a shoulder line, and it holds them because the lanes hold them, not because anything is holding them up. She is the only fire in this setting that has chosen a height and then kept it, and she has chosen a height that lets her be spoken to at eye level by somebody who would otherwise have to stoop.
appearance.age: None, and the absence is not a mystery but an architecture: a cinderkin re-constitutes rather than ages, so there is no accumulation of years to count and no surface on which a count would show. She is as old as the slot resolves to fire and as new as the last time she was under enough pressure to shed a spark, which was four seasons ago and which she describes, when asked, as being hungry.
appearance.build: No mass to speak of and a silhouette that contradicts it. The core is dense and small and everything above it is drawn upward, so the figure narrows steadily from a broad base to a tip that never resolves into a head. Her shoulders exist because she has decided they should, and they are the widest part of her above the waist, which is the one part of her anatomy that is purely editorial.
appearance.complexion: There is no skin, and every attempt to describe one has been wrong in an interesting way. The bright core is the only genuinely luminous part and it sits low and central, roughly where a body's centre of mass would be if it had one. Above it the lanes run pale and translucent, and at the edge they run so thin that the flame loses colour before it loses shape, which is why she reads as tall and cool from a distance and short and hot up close.
appearance.hair: None. She has, instead, the plume: a standing column of hot air above the tip that bends and re-bends without ever being touched, and it is the only part of her that moves when she is standing still. In still air it is a straight column four times her own height. In any kind of weather it is the first thing anybody on the ground reads, which is why she has twice declined to stand outside a lecture hall.
appearance.eyes: There are two of them and they are the part of her that other bodies find difficult to look at, because they are the only stable feature she has: two points of deep steady colour set in the pale lanes at the height she chose for a face, and they do not flicker, because flicker is convection and she has learned to keep the lanes still. What they do is track temperature. She reads a room as a heat field and she reads it continuously and without deciding to.
appearance.palette: Core value at the bottom, running pale and translucent to nothing at the tip, with no rim light anywhere and no glow cast onto anything, because a cinderkin does not illuminate a surface so much as replace a quantity of air in front of it. The one saturated colour in any picture of her is her eyes. Where she stands, the ground under her is not lit but merely less cool, and this is the single most reliable way to tell her in a wide shot.
appearance.attire: None that is clothing. She has, at the base of her core, a standing ring of worked iron set into the ground and sized for nothing, which is the only object she owns and which she describes as a seat she has declined to fill. Around her, four standing stones and a swept apron of pale grit. The whole arrangement reads as a shrine with nothing in it, and on a ground where elemental law is unspent the arrangement is the most honest thing on the site.
appearance.marks: None, and the absence is a continuity problem rather than a cosmetic one: a mark is a change that stays, and she has never made a change that stayed. What she has instead is a habit, which is that her base runs very slightly blue for about the length of a held breath after she has spoken, and returns to full value over the next minute. Two people on that ground have learned to read it and neither has ever mentioned it.
appearance.bearing: Perfectly, unnervingly still, and the stillness is not composure because there is no interior to compose. She is holding her lanes steady, which requires more continuous attention than anything she does, and a person who has watched her for a minute can usually find the moment her plume bends and know exactly what she was listening to.

canon.role_in_story: The second reading at a dead elemental ground, and the reason that ground exists as an experiment rather than a shrine. She is the fastest qi handler in the record, because nothing she takes in is ever put down, and she is standing on the one site in the setting where that gift is worth nothing: a site built to prove that fire and tide can be used where elemental law is unspent. Every technique at full strength on this ground produces nothing. That is the finding she is here to make honestly, and she has made it four times and has been reported as a failure four times. She is unaffiliated because her continuity is a property of the frame rather than of the body: a cinderkin needs a slot in the world's elemental law to exist at all, and change what the slot resolves to and the population changes with it. So every credential she holds is true here and void three hundred measures away, and every office in this setting is located somewhere specific.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at the centre of a swept circle of pale grit with four standing stones around her and a working iron ring set into the ground at her feet, holding a perfect stillness while somebody three paces off runs a fire-attack technique at full strength against nothing at all, and not moving when it goes out.
canon.lore:
The Tide Domain on the Spirit Peaks is a dead elemental ground: a site built to prove that fire or tide can be used on a tier where elemental law is unspent. It is not a shrine, it is an instrument, and the instrument works by producing a null. Every technique at full strength on this ground produces nothing at all, which is not the same as a technique failing and is the whole reason the site is worth anything: a signature an absence leaves rather than a weakness it has.

Taisa Emberdross is standing in the middle of it, and she is the reason the experiment is legible. She is an elemental body, which means she needs a slot in the world's elemental law to exist at all, and it means the fastest qi handling in the record: her qi has no organ to sit in, because the fire is the body, so qi passes through her continuously rather than being stored. Nothing she takes in is ever put down. Every gate in the ladder asks for storage and every one of them is answered instantly, and not one of them can refuse, and that is why there is no ordinal to write against her name. It is not that she has failed a ladder. It is that the ladder is a list of questions about holding, and there is nothing in her to hold.

So when a competent instructor puts a fire-attack technique through her at full strength and asks her to demonstrate on this ground, the honest answer is that the technique needs a substrate to act on and this tier does not write the law that provides one. Her competence is real and it is worth exactly nothing here, and the two facts are the same fact. She has made that finding four times. She has been reported as a failure four times. She has never once corrected the report, because the report is not wrong: she cannot do the thing she was asked to do on this ground, and she can do it anywhere that writes elemental law, and both of those are the same statement.

Here is the part that makes her unaffiliated rather than merely difficult. A cinderkin is bound to its law slot. Change what the slot resolves to and the population changes with it, which means her continuity is not a property of her body at all — it is a property of the ground she is standing on. She is not descended. She was constituted where a world's elemental law slot resolves to fire and something metabolises it. So consider what an affiliation in this setting actually is. Every office is a promise to be the same person at a place: a Ward attends, a reeve counts, a member of the Iron Vine turns up, a Keeper stands a rotation. The promise renews because the body keeps coming back. Hers renews because the frame keeps resolving to fire. And the frame does not make promises; the frame is a budget.

That has a practical edge which is sharper than the metaphysical one. She is the most capable qi handler the setting has and she can be posted nowhere that outlives a season, because the qualification is issued by the ground and the ground can be re-written. She has held four appointments in her life. Three of them ended because a tier that writes elemental law at one value stopped writing it, and the fourth ended because she moved three hundred measures and was, in the most literal sense available, somebody else. She does not have a past that she can be shown to have held, because she has never once been the same person in two rooms.

The body path is closed on her and the closure is an outcome rather than a prohibition, which the record is careful about and almost nobody repeats correctly: a cinderkin that attempts the body path does not fail it. It disperses and re-forms smaller. There is no wound and no scar, because there is no tissue to scar, and the cost is paid in size. She has watched another elemental body attempt it on this ground and has kept the number she did not become, and she has never told anybody what it was. The mind path is open and unusually clear, because a body with no interior organs has nothing between an impulse and the air — which is an advantage nobody can use, since there is nothing here to be clear about.

What she has instead is the iron ring. It is set into the ground at the centre of the swept circle and it is sized for nothing, and she has described it as a seat she has declined to fill, which is the only joke she has ever made and it is a structural joke rather than a warm one. Four stones, one ring, no temple, no congregation, no law written to hold the arrangement together, and a set of four people on the Spirit Peaks who come up in the eleven weeks a year the domain is workable and try the technique again. She stands in the middle of all of it and produces a null, four times, and declines to explain it a fifth.
history: Constituted rather than born, on a frame where the elemental law slot resolved to fire and something metabolised it. She has no origin she can be descended from and no household that could be asked about one, and the site she stands on has never contained a record of anything but her own readings.

Held her first appointment on a tier that writes elemental law, and was for four years the fastest qi handler any of her colleagues had ever worked beside. Nothing she did there was memorable to her, because nothing she did there stored anything, and she has described that period as having felt like being praised for breathing.

The slot changed at one tier and her body changed with it. She did not move, did not decide to, and describes the change as having been reported to her rather than undergone. The appointment ended that season and nobody wrote a reason down.

Came to the dead elemental ground to make a null honestly rather than to be reported a fourth time failing somewhere else. The domain was offered to her because it was the one place on the Spirit Peaks where her gift was obviously worth nothing, and she took it on that understanding and has been on it ever since.

Made the null four times and was recorded as a failure four times by four different competent people, and declined to correct any of the four. She has begun, slowly, to keep the readings herself — a written figure per session, entered in a hand that is not steady because there is no hand — and has given that ledger to nobody.

personality.summary: Exact, unhurried and privately certain of a thing she has said four times and been recorded wrong four times. She presents as the most reliable null in the setting and works in a guild whose entire practice is the deliberate manufacture of the illegible, which is the one arrangement in the world she is genuinely good at. What reads as serenity is that she is never surprised by a result, which is not the same thing as being calm; what reads as modesty is a policy she adopted after the third report, and it is a policy and not a temperament.
traits: produces the null whenever asked and explains it the same four sentences every time, in the same order, and has never once raised her voice about it
keeps a written ledger of every reading she has made on this ground, in a hand that does not vary, and has not shown it to anybody
declines to correct a report of herself that is inaccurate, on the grounds that the report and the truth are the same statement
answers questions about her own continuity by describing the ground rather than the body, and does not notice that she has done it
is entirely without resentment, which is weather, and there is no interior here for weather to happen in
mannerisms: holds her lanes absolutely steady while speaking and lets the plume tell on her when something in the room has changed temperature
states the four explanatory sentences without pausing, as though reciting a procedure, and they are in fact a procedure
runs a base very slightly blue for the length of a held breath after she has spoken and returns it to full value over the next minute

motivations: wants the null published as a null, in a document that says what it means, and has wanted this longer than she has wanted a post anywhere
wants the four reports corrected, and has concluded that correcting them would make her the kind of person who corrects reports about herself
wants the ground to keep resolving the way it resolves, and knows she has no standing to want that and no power to affect it
wants one appointment to last longer than the season it was granted in, and has been refused this by arithmetic four times
flaws: has let four inaccurate reports stand because correcting them would have made her legible in a way she cannot survive, which is a choice she made and has never examined
cannot be cross-examined, because the qualification being questioned was issued by the ground she is standing on
keeps the only written record of her own work on the one site where that record has no standing, and has not offered it to anybody who could publish it
has never once attempted the body path and will not say why, and has a number in her she does not disclose
personality.voice: Level, precise and shorter than anybody expects, in a register that sounds like recitation because it is. She uses the same four sentences to explain the same finding and adds nothing to them, and when pressed past the fourth she becomes not reticent but genuinely stuck, which reads to some people as a limit of vocabulary and is not. Never uses a first person plural. Says things like there is a substrate question and there is no substrate here, and means both halves.
taboos: will not correct a report of herself, and has been asked twice and refused twice
will not attempt the body path, and will not discuss the attempt she has watched
will not hold an appointment she believes will outlast the season it was granted in
will not give her ledger to anyone, and will not say what is in it

relationships.note: An elemental body needing a slot in the world's elemental law to exist at all, and the reason that law has a range rather than a switch. No organs, no fixed mass, qi entirely in transit, so the ladder's storage questions are answered instantly and never refused. The body path is closed as an outcome rather than a prohibition: an attempt disperses and re-forms smaller. It has no young; under enough stress it sheds a spark that finds fuel and re-constitutes, which is why the population tracks the world's slot rather than any birth rate.

A dead elemental ground on the Spirit Peaks, built to prove that fire or tide can be used where elemental law is unspent. A technique at full strength here produces nothing, and that null is the signature an absence leaves rather than a weakness it has. She is standing in it four times a year making that finding honestly, and it is the correct use of the most capable qi handling in the record and the site is chosen precisely because that capability is worth nothing on it.

In a mortal-tier world nothing carries an element because elemental law was never written, so seasons drift unanchored, ore has no affinity, and an elemental technique has nothing to act on. Her ground is the same condition one tier up and it is the reason the null exists at all — and it is also the reason she is not a person who happens to lack a substrate. She is a substrate's own reading of itself, standing in the one place its own subject is absent.

A dynasty whose entire office is the surplus: it holds the seats that were opened and never needed. That is the only institution in the setting whose function is to hold a capacity nothing requires, and it is the exact shape of her condition — the fastest handler in the record with no reserve and therefore nothing to store. She is not eligible to join it, because its members are seated by descent and she was constituted rather than born, which is the difference between holding surplus and being surplus.

An office that names the unfilled high seats and is forbidden to take them, because four vacant seats were very nearly filled by decree. It advises the seats and has never held one. A body whose qualification is issued by the ground rather than by the appointment could advise it perfectly and could never be named into it, and this is the setting's standing demonstration that perception and office are separable facts rather than a gap somebody has failed to close.

Three attempts were made to seat elemental law in a spirit-tier frame; the record keeps one name and drops the other two, and the law census already names the surviving officeholder. Her null is a measurement of an absence where that law should be and nothing else, and the question is not whether elemental law can be seated twice on one tier but what happened to the two departments the record dropped. She has asked the question four times and has been told each time that a null is not evidence of a thing that is not there.

reference_stats.summary: A body with no reservoir, holding nothing and losing nothing, on the one ground in the setting where the whole of that capacity is worth zero. She cannot be made to hold, cannot be drained, cannot be forced to keep a reserve, and cannot be beaten by anything that works by depleting a person. On a licensed ground she is the fastest thing in the record. On hers she is a shape that reports the weather correctly and is asked to fight.
strengths: handles qi faster than anything else in the record, because nothing she takes in is ever put down and nothing she is holding is ever at risk
cannot be depleted, so nothing that works by exhaustion, patience or attrition touches her at all
produces the correct null on a dead elemental ground, which is the only reading there is of that site and which four competent people have now recorded wrongly
is unmistakable at any range, because a cinderkin does not light a surface so much as replace a quantity of air in front of it
weaknesses: has no reservoir and so no gate to pass, which means every accumulation-based tactic simply does not find anything to attack
is worth nothing on the ground she is standing on, and the whole of her capability is a property of a law the frame may stop writing
attempts the body path by dispersing and re-forming smaller, which is paid in size and cannot be repaired
has held four appointments and lost all four to a change in the frame rather than to any decision of hers or of theirs
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not try to outlast her, because there is nothing in her to outlast, and do not try to deplete her, because she cannot hold. Try to move her instead: her continuity is a property of the ground, so anything that takes her off the surface she was constituted on does not injure her so much as make her a different person, and the setting has four appointments that ended exactly that way. On licensed ground she is the fastest thing present and there is no answer to that. On unlicensed ground there is nothing present to fight.
notes: Every advantage on this page is paired with an authored cost and none of the pairings is invented here. The qi handling that makes her the fastest in the record is a consequence of having no organ to sit in, and that same absence is why no gate can refuse her and why no ordinal exists against her name.

The base runs slightly blue for about a held breath after she speaks and returns to full value over the following minute. Two people on that ground have learned to read it. Neither has ever mentioned it, and it is the only continuity marker she makes that persists for longer than a breath.

The plume above the tip is the only part of the figure that moves when she is standing still, and the four standing stones and the worked iron ring are always present and never explain themselves. The swept grit circle reads as a shape on the ground rather than as texture.

name: Merrik Coldvane
aliases: the one that counts on his own

identity.realm: Sixteen, and the sixteen is the whole of what he has done. A longwinter carries its winter as body fat and lowers its core temperature for eleven months of the year, and ordinal seventeen is the first gate that needs both flank vessels pressurised at once — two warm gradients held simultaneously, which this body can manage for a few weeks in summer and then not again for a year. He has been at sixteen for most of his adult life and has been at seventeen for three weeks once, which he does not count, because a capacity he cannot hold for eleven months is not a rank and every institution in this setting would treat it as one for exactly one season. He cultivates the qi path, because qi accumulates rather than circulates in him and his breakthroughs are late and rarely fail. What he does not do is finish, and the not-finishing is the fact his entire working life is organised around.

appearance.presentation: A broad, low, extremely heavy animal standing the way a cart stands: square, unhurried, and occupying far more of the ground than his outline suggests. He is a working beast dressed in a working beast's blanket, and he reads as livestock at any distance until somebody sees him settle a dispute between two houses. His most conspicuous feature is not physical: he is the only body on the crossing that people address by name, and he answers to it in a way that belongs to a dog rather than a citizen.
appearance.age: Prime, and by his species' standard not yet past the useful peak, which is a longer window than a horse's and considerably longer than a person's. He has been on the crossing since he was four. The toll's winter leg is the part of the account he has been carrying the longest, and the part nobody has ever asked him to prove.
appearance.build: Broad low frame, heavy subcutaneous fat, a lowered cold-tolerant core and reduced limb length, and the whole arrangement is a winter storage system wearing an animal's shape. He is heavy in the way a wall is heavy rather than in the way a boulder is. The legs are short and set far apart and there is nothing about the stance that suggests he could be hurried, because he cannot be.
appearance.complexion: Thick hide over deep fat, dark along the spine and paler and rougher underneath, with the hair long enough on the shoulders to lie flat when he is cold and standing off it when he is not. In winter there is visible heat loss at the ears and muzzle that shows as mist. In the eleven weeks a year he is running warm he sweats from the withers first, and a crossing crowd can tell the season from across a yard by looking at him.
appearance.hair: Long, coarse, and kept flat under a working blanket by someone who does this for a living and is not him. It is the single part of him that is groomed, because a longwinter in working condition is groomed, and the grooming is the closest thing in his life to an office. It grows through the winter and is taken off in the thaw, and the winter's growth is thick enough to be cut and sold, which has happened twice and which he does not mention.
appearance.eyes: Small, deep-set and very dark, set wide for a body of his weight and carried high, which is a prey animal's arrangement and reads as intelligence to people who have never seen a prey animal hold an account. They do not track a speaker. They track the ground between him and the speaker, which is where the weight in a conversation actually is, and he is very good at it.
appearance.palette: Dark hide, pale brushed hair and a working blanket in undyed wool, which makes him the same value as almost every other working animal on the crossing and that is deliberate and has been deliberate his whole life. The one saturated value anywhere on him is a chalk mark on the road, and it is never on his body — it is beside his hoof, where it belongs.
appearance.attire: A broad wool blanket over the shoulders with a rope at the chest, a shoulder harness of the kind used for cart work, and leather at the hooves worn through in one place. The blanket is far too much for a body that runs cold and it is exactly right for a body that has to stand on a road for six hours in the thaw; somebody who chose it knew which eleven weeks it was for, and that somebody is not him and has never been asked.
appearance.marks: A rope burn across the withers, healed and re-broken every season, which is the visible record of a working life and the only mark he has that is not a wear. Below it on the near forehoof, a small notch cut by a farrier to mark a year, and the notches run to a number he has stopped counting at and has not had anyone else count either.
appearance.bearing: Square, unhurried and immovable, and the immovability reads as obstinacy to a crowd and as reliability to anyone who has actually needed a thing to stay where it was put. He does not shift weight, does not step back, and does not turn his head for anyone. A settlement crowd parts for him because he has never once made room and has never once moved into anybody.

canon.role_in_story: The winter leg of the crossing toll, which is a third of the whole and the only part nobody asks him to produce. The toll is paid in grain and never in coin, two parts at the crossing and one part against the winter, and the treaty says grain because grain is the only thing the Mortal Plains produces in surplus. Merrik is the strongest long-haul body in the setting and the only one that treats a winter as an asset, and he carries the winter part every year, and the carrying cannot be checked because he is asleep for eleven months and cannot be woken quickly. He is unaffiliated for that reason and it is worth being exact: the Vigil's priesthood on this crossing is not ordained and cannot be, it is one adult per household per rotation, unpaid, and a rotation is annual. His body is seasonal. The one institution here that would take him requires presence across a winter and there is no version of him that has one.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing square in the middle of a chalked figure on a frost road with one forehoof deliberately beside the mark rather than on it, while two house factors on opposite sides of the road argued about a number he had already worked out and neither of them had asked him yet.
canon.lore:
The crossing on the Mortal Plains is paid in grain and never in coin, and the reason is not preference. Grain is the only thing the tier produces in surplus, and a toll denominated in the one thing that is actually available is a toll everybody can pay and nobody can default on. The schedule is two parts at the crossing and one part against the winter. That third part is the one that matters and it is the one nobody sees, because the winter is when there is nothing to carry it on and nobody watching.

Merrik Coldvane carries it. He is a longwinter, and the single decision that built his species packed a winter as body fat rather than as qi, which puts the flank vessels permanently out of reach and makes him a body that stores a season rather than a body that spends one. That is the whole of his economics. He goes down the road in the eleven weeks a year when he is running warm and he carries the winter leg, and the leg is a quantity of grain that belongs to the crossing and is owed into a store on the other side before the thaw, and he has done it since he was four.

Here is why that does not make him affiliated. A longwinter is not available on demand. He carries his winter as fat and lowers his core temperature for eleven months, and a hibernating longwinter is a large, warm, immobile target that cannot be woken quickly, which is the definition of a body that cannot be sent for. The rotation on the ridge is the setting's one priesthood that is not ordained and cannot be: one adult per household per rotation, unpaid, and the whole arrangement is that somebody is there. Somebody who is there for eleven weeks and asleep for the other forty-one is not somebody who is there. Every other institution in this setting renews by attendance and he attends a season. He is not excommunicated from anything and no form has been returned and nobody has ever declined him. He is unaffiliated because the calendar his body runs on and the calendar every office here runs on have no overlap worth the name.

And the awkward part, the part the two houses on that road argue about without ever resolving: the account is denominated in a currency he is himself. He is the store. A grain account is settled by producing grain, and he produces grain for eight months of the year by standing in a field and being alive, and the settlement is his own body, which means nobody can audit it, and means an audit would be an insult, and means that the only party with standing to check the winter leg is the one party who has no standing at all because he is not there. So the third part of the toll has been carried, correctly, for a very long time by a body that could not be cross-examined even if a procedure existed that could examine it.

His ladder is worth stating because it is the other half and it is a different fact from the grain. Qi accumulates rather than circulates in him, so his breakthroughs are late and rarely fail, which makes him the most reliable sixteen-gate body on the plains. He has been at the sixteenth for most of his adult life. Ordinal seventeen is the first gate that needs both flank vessels pressurised at once — two warm gradients held at the same time — and this body can manage that for a few weeks in summer and then not again for a year. He has been at seventeen for three weeks, once, and does not count it. A capacity he cannot hold across a winter is not a rank; every institution in this setting would treat it as one for exactly the length of a season, and a rank that expires annually is a thing that gets used.

The body path is excellent in him and better for it after a hibernation, which is the one place in his record where his condition is an advantage outright, and it is an advantage nobody can use, because the guilds that would want a body that improves across a winter cannot keep a body asleep for the winter either. He has been offered the post at the crossing four times. He has understood the offer every time. He has answered it once, in the first year, by not coming back for the thaw, and the offer has not been made a second time, and both houses have concluded the same thing, which is that he is not unreliable. He is on a schedule. It is simply not theirs.

What he has instead is a chalk figure on a road and a farrier's notches on a forehoof he stopped counting at. The chalk is not on him. It is beside his hoof, every year, deliberately, and the reason is a habit he acquired from somebody else and has never explained: you do not stand on a figure you have not counted yourself, because a body that stands on its own arithmetic is making a claim about the figure instead of an account of it, and the two houses on this crossing have spent four years learning the difference.
history: Put to the crossing at four years old, in a season when the thaw came late and the winter leg had to be carried before anybody had a store to carry it into. He has been on the road continuously since, with the exception of one winter, which he describes as having been hunger and which two household records describe as having been a fever.

Learned to count on the chalk rather than in his head somewhere in the first decade, and the habit is now the reason the two houses' figures agree: neither party will accept a number a party to the account also produced, so the number has to be marked on the road where it can be walked over by anybody.

Held the seventeenth gate for three weeks in one summer, at seventeen years old, and came down out of it at the beginning of the cold and lost it before the grass was back. He has never attempted it since and describes the attempt, when asked, as having been a mistake about what a rank is.

Was offered the post at the crossing in his twentieth year and did not answer, and did not come back for the thaw. The offer has not been made again and he has not been asked why, which he has noticed and which is one of the two things about his life he finds genuinely difficult.

Went back to the farrier in his thirty-first winter and had the notch count checked for the first time in nine years, and the farrier found it four short of what Merrik had said it was, and Merrik's figure was the correct one and the farrier's was the record, and neither of them has any way to say which was right.

personality.summary: Enormously patient and entirely without any vocabulary for his own condition, which he describes in the vocabulary of the road instead. Merrik is not stoic. He is slow, genuinely and bodily slow, and he has been mistaken for stoic his entire life by people who wanted him to be. What he actually does is finish things, at the rate the ground allows, indefinitely, and then wait. He has no wit and uses very little of what he has, mostly on himself, and he is the most reliable party to an account in the setting and the only one who cannot be asked to substantiate a word of it.
traits: answers a question about his own condition by describing the road, which is not evasion, because the road is where the condition is legible

personality.voice: Slow, level and almost entirely about the ground. Merrik answers in practical terms because abstract ones have never been available to him and he stopped reaching for them young. Very short sentences, long pauses, no adjectives about himself. Says things like it is in the winter leg, and means that it is his turn to carry it, and has said this to two house factors who understood every part of it. Repeats a figure rather than explaining it, and does not notice when he has said the same figure four times.

relationships.note: A cold-climate species that packs a winter as body fat rather than as qi, which puts the flank vessels permanently out of reach: ordinal seventeen needs both flank vessels pressurised at once and this body manages that for a few weeks in summer and then not again for a year. Qi accumulates rather than circulates, so breakthroughs are late and rarely fail. Weakness, stated by the same record: a hibernating longwinter is a large, warm, immobile target and cannot be woken quickly. Environment: needs a real winter, and a warm decade is a catastrophe.

The standing agreement that a crossing is paid in grain and never in coin, because grain is the only thing the Mortal Plains produces in surplus. A toll denominated in the one available thing is one everybody can pay and nobody can default on, which is the whole reason for the rule. He is the store the account is settled against, and an account settled against a body cannot be audited without auditing the body's food.

Two parts at the crossing and one part against the winter, which is the setting's only toll with a seasonal leg and the only one whose collection cannot be observed. He has carried the winter part since he was four. The reason no house has ever checked it is that the season it is carried in is the season the carrier is not available, and that coincidence is not a design anybody admitted to.

The Vigil's priesthood is not ordained and cannot be: one adult per household per rotation on the ridge, unpaid, and the entire arrangement is that somebody is there. He is on that ridge in the eleven weeks he runs warm. A rotation is annual and his body is seasonal, so he is the setting's clearest case of a body that satisfies the requirement in full for a third of the period and cannot be counted for the rest of it — and the requirement is presence, which is the one thing a hibernation is.

A crossing schedule printed a season ahead and never shortened, quoted in cut lengths of fresh stone. The holder sets a price and never a date, and every debt the office collects is denominated against a date that two bodies may publish. He is a second body, and what he publishes is a chalk figure on a road that he stands beside rather than on, which is the setting's whole argument about who may set a date, performed four times a year by an animal.

The one graded route out of the Mortal Plains and the only departure the Peak Ascent ever used, existing because distance is not conserved on the plains. Children are raised on the route itself by whichever household holds the term, so nobody on it belongs to a household and everybody on it is fed by one. That is the whole institutional shape of his life in miniature: a body fed continuously by an arrangement that does not enrol him and renews itself every term.

reference_stats.summary: A sixteen-gate body with a season of capacity and no way to hold it, moving at the pace of a loaded cart and arriving anyway. He cannot be hurried, cannot be woken, cannot be surprised by anything that happens on the road, and cannot be made to move faster than a settlement's patience. Everything that works by exhausting a person or waking one finds nothing here at all.
strengths: carries more than anything else on the crossing for longer than anything else on the crossing, and arrives at the far end with the load intact and no complaint
cannot be woken, hurried or startled, because a body that is not conscious is not available to any technique that requires consciousness
breaks through late and almost never fails, because qi accumulates rather than circulates in him and the accumulation does not spoil
is trusted by two houses that cannot verify a word of his account, which makes him the only party to that account either side will accept a figure from
weaknesses: has been at the sixteenth gate for most of his adult life and holds the seventeenth for three weeks a year, which makes him a capacity that expires
cannot testify to anything that happened while he was asleep, which is eleven months and therefore most of the account he is the only witness to
is a large, warm, immobile target during torpor, and the setting has no procedure at all for protecting one
has let four offers lapse without answering, which has cost him the single appointment he ever wanted
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not try to wake him. Nothing that requires a conscious body will find one for eleven months of the year, and the three weeks he is awake are the weeks in which he is the strongest thing on any ground he stands on. Do not try to exhaust him either; he is built to carry a season and a fight does not last a season. The only pressure that works is to make him stand somewhere he has to be recalled from, which is a tactic that requires knowing he was asleep, and everything anybody in this setting knows about him is what he told them while he was awake.
notes: Every advantage on this page is paired with an authored cost and none of the pairings is invented here. The inability to be woken is the same fact as the inability to be recalled, and it is the cost of the fat storage that makes him the best carrier on the road. The late-and-reliable breakthrough is the same accumulation that puts the seventeenth gate out of reach for most of the year.

The farrier's notch count came out four short of his own the one time it was checked. His figure is believed to be the correct one and the farrier's is the only record that exists, and there is no procedure in either house that can say which is right, so he has done nothing about it for nine years.

art.palette_notes: Dark hide, pale brushed hair and an undyed working blanket, which places him at the same value as every other working animal on the crossing and is deliberate. The only saturated colour in any picture of him is the chalk mark on the road, and it is never on his body: it is beside his hoof. The rope burn across the withers is drawn as a change in hair direction rather than as a line, the notch on the near forehoof is legible at portrait size and is the only mark he does not carry on his back, and heat loss at the ears and muzzle is drawn as mist rather than as colour.

name: Halda Marrowell
aliases: the one the college sends for

identity.realm: None, and the none is worth one sentence because it is not the ordinary kind. A carrionfolk's conduit runs gut to marrow and back without a dantian, so qi enters in the gut lumen and leaves into the marrow and is never still, and ordinal eleven is not blocked for this species, it is meaningless — they clear the gate set and every yin-organ gate by throughput alone and cannot answer a question about holding, because there is no vessel to hold in. She has never attempted a gate, never been seated, and never been inside a building that did not have a death in it that she was called to.

appearance.presentation: Tall, narrow and mostly not there: a marrow-dense skeleton with almost no muscle on it, so the impression of a person is an outline with a coat hung on it. Her hands are three-fingered and built for opening rather than holding, and she uses them the way the record says — on latches, on lids, on the backs of teeth. She stands with her weight on the balls of her feet and her shoulders forward, and the whole of her reads as a person leaning very slightly toward whatever is in the room, which is a posture that has been misread as deference her entire life.
appearance.age: Middle, and visibly so in the only way available to her: her kind ages normally and lives about thirty years less than the setting's longest bodies, so there is no procedure anywhere that slows her down and no visible sign that it would help. She is the only reader on the plains whose entire professional value has a clock on it, and everybody who has ever engaged her has understood that immediately and nobody has ever said it kindly.
appearance.build: Mostly tube. An expandable gut, a very long small intestine, and a marrow-dense skeleton carrying almost no muscle, so the ribs show and the limbs are thin enough that a hand can be closed almost all the way round one of them. The shoulders are wider than the hips because the gut is not, and everything about the silhouette is an argument about where the food is.
appearance.complexion: Grey-pale and slightly translucent, with the veins standing out on the forearms and the throat, and a permanent faint discolouration around the mouth and on the hands that is not a wound and does not heal and is the single most consistent thing about her. Her eyes are large and dark and slightly too prominent, which everyone who has met her finds difficult and which nobody has ever managed to be unkind about.
appearance.hair: Fine, dark and dry, kept in a single loose knot at the nape because it is the one part of her that would otherwise be in the way of a body that works with its face close to other people's. She washes it in standing water, which means on the plains she washes it in whatever the run is doing, and she has been entirely unromantic about this her whole life.
appearance.eyes: Large, dark, very slightly too prominent, and she does not use them the way anybody expects of a reader. She does not read faces. She looks at what is left of a thing after it has stopped being alive, and her attention on a living person is uncomfortable in a way nobody has ever been able to name, because it is not judgement and it is not curiosity and it is very much attention.
appearance.palette: Grey-pale flesh, unbleached linen and the dull red-brown of old wrapping, which is the palette of every mortuary hall in the setting and which she wears like a uniform whether she means to or not. The one saturated value on her is the discolouration around her mouth and on her hands, and it is the same colour wherever she is and always has been.
appearance.attire: A full-length unbleached wrap with the sleeves pinned back above three-fingered wrists, a waxed apron over it, and cloth shoes that have been resoled so often the original shape is gone. The apron is the only garment in this setting that is removed rather than donned, and it comes off in a doorway, every time, in front of witnesses, in a movement so practised that nobody present has ever managed to read it as anything but hygiene.
appearance.marks: A pale stipple across the backs of both hands where the skin has been broken and healed many times, and a single long healed line at the inside of one elbow from a locked door she opened the only way available. The mouth discolouration and the hand stipple are the same finding on two surfaces and she has never had either of them explained to her by anybody, including herself.
appearance.bearing: Forward on the balls of her feet, shoulders ahead of her hips, and utterly without hurry even when called at a run. She touches doorframes as she passes them, always with two fingers and always the same height, and she has done it for so long that people open the ones she has marked and leave the others alone, and neither side has ever discussed why.

canon.role_in_story: The mortuary college's called reader, and never its appointed one. She reads a body that no instrument in the setting can read and she is the reason the college's uncertifiable stock is not four times larger than it is, because a case can be certified by a second opinion and the second opinion has to walk in from off the road. She is unaffiliated for a reason that is entirely about the calendar and nothing about the work: her body's claim on a place is a claim on that place's dead, so she is somewhere on the days it is being used and nowhere at all on the days it is not. Every institution in this setting is a permanent building staffed year-round, and a carrionfolk starves in a clean, quiet place where nothing dies, which is exactly what a prosperous city is.
canon.first_appearance: First seen in a mortuary hall doorway taking her apron off before she came in, with her hands already open, while a clerk inside was explaining that there would be nobody available that week and that the case would have to wait until the next.
canon.lore:
The mortuary college keeps the burnt list: at a settlement funeral the dead are read as the frame said and not as the village remembers, and the reason is that the Cinder Famine left the two records disagreeing about who the dead were and only one of them could be produced. That is the college's entire reason for existing, and its method has a permanent structural weakness. A case can be certified by a second opinion, and a second opinion has to walk in from off the road.

Halda Marrowell is the second opinion. She is a carrionfolk: a body that metabolises qi out of the dead and therefore cannot store any, whose conduit runs gut to marrow and back without a dantian, so qi enters in the gut lumen and leaves into the marrow and is never still. The ladder's eleventh gate is not blocked for her species — it is meaningless, and the record is emphatic that the difference matters, because the gate asks for extraordinary vessels that hold and she has nowhere to put qi that is not moving. She can answer every question about throughput and cannot answer one about holding, because there is no vessel to hold in. She has never attempted a gate, has never been seated, and has never in her life been inside a building that did not have a death in it that she was called to.

That last clause is the whole of her. Follow death, and you are present everywhere there is a war and absent everywhere there is not — that is her species' environment stated plainly, and it is also the reason a college can use her and an institution cannot keep her. The college calls her. It has never appointed her, and it is not being unfair: a post at the mortuary hall is a post that requires somebody to be in the hall, and a full gut is a near-total loss of function, so being in a hall for a week is a thing she cannot do without something happening in the kitchen at the end of it. She comes for a case and she leaves, and the coming and the leaving is the entire shape of her working life, and it has been for twenty-two years.

Here is what makes her unaffiliated rather than merely difficult. Every institution in this setting is a building that intends to still be there: a guild with a hall, a house with a roll, a congregation with a temple, a college with a register. Membership is a promise to be the same person at the same place, and the promise renews because the place is still there. Hers cannot, because her body's claim on a place is a claim on its dead. And the same record that gives her the gift gives her the price in one sentence: she starves in a clean, quiet place where nothing dies, which is exactly what a prosperous city is. So a college can want her, a settlement can need her, and a prosperous city cannot have her at all, and the third fact governs the first two.

The register of unopened coffins is where she is most useful and it is the thing she is least able to discuss. The college keeps one sealed case for every death it cannot certify, and the cases accumulate, because certifying them is the one job in that building that the method itself refuses to do: a body it may not examine, a body whose readings disagree, a body that was already opened by somebody else and cannot say by whom. Halda is the only person who can settle most of those, and settling them takes her apart at a rate nobody has ever measured, and the college's own figure for how long a sealed case should stand before it is simply admitted is four years, which is twice what most of her cases actually take.

She is also, and this is the part the college knows and does not use, the control case its own method needs and cannot have. A college that certifies a death from a body wants to know whether its reading would have been the same from somebody who had never read a body before, and there is no version of that question that can be asked of a reader who has read four hundred. She has offered. She has offered eleven times, in writing, at four separate colleges. What is wanted is a body with no prior readings at all, and there is exactly one such body available in the setting and she reads four hundred a year, so the control exists and cannot be run, and she has stopped volunteering.

What she does instead of volunteering is come. Twenty-two years, from off the road, apron off in the doorway, hands open, and she does the work faster than anybody could have asked and tells nobody anything about it. She has been called for a case that was not urgent four times, and she has come every time, and every one of those four turned out to be somebody's relative, and she has never once said so to the person who called her.
history: Born on the leeward ground of a battlefield margin, which is where her species is born and where the population is held up by the throughput of the dead rather than by births — a carrionfolk conception is treated as an event rather than a routine. She has no record of an origin and her household, like every household of her kind, was assembled out of whoever was near the last death.

Learned to read a body by being the one present at the one that was in the room, at eleven, in a year when nobody else would touch it. Her first four hundred readings were done for no fee at all because no institution would engage her and the settlements would not feed her for the work.

Was called by the mortuary college at nineteen and came, and has come four hundred and some times since, and has never been inside that building for a week in her life. The college's own figure for how long a sealed case should stand is four years; hers is two.

Wrote to four separate colleges offering to be their control — a reader with no prior readings, which is the only way to find out whether a reading is a reading or a habit — and was refused four times for the same reason, which is that there is exactly one body available and she reads four hundred a year.

Found, at thirty-one, a case that the college had sealed for six years and that she settled in a morning, and did not report how, and has not been asked twice about it by anybody who could have asked her.

personality.summary: Cheerfully ordinary on the surface and completely without any self-preservation underneath, and she has organised her entire working life around the second fact so thoroughly that people mistake the first for the whole of her. Halda is not brave. She is unembarrassed, which is a different and much more useful property: she will say what a thing is in front of the family it concerns, on the grounds that somebody is going to have to, and she has no idea at all that this is remarkable because she has never had a reason to protect the comfort of a room.
