relationships.note: A body that metabolises qi out of the dead and therefore cannot store any. The conduit runs gut to marrow and back without a dantian, so ordinal eleven is not blocked for this species, it is meaningless, which is the record's own distinction: they clear the gate set by throughput alone and cannot answer a question about holding because there is no vessel to hold in. A full gut is a near-total loss of function, and a carrionfolk starves in a clean, quiet place where nothing dies, which is exactly what a prosperous city is.

The college that keeps the burnt list, reading the dead as the frame said rather than as the village remembers because the two records disagreed about who the dead were after the Cinder Famine. Its method has one structural weakness: a case is certified by a second opinion, and a second opinion has to walk in from off the road. She is that opinion, four hundred times, and has never held a post in the building because a post requires presence and her presence is a function of a death rate.

One sealed case for every death the college cannot certify, and the cases accumulate because certifying them is the one job the method itself refuses to do. It is the only growing stock in the setting that does not fill at a rate set by the living, and she is the only person who can settle most of it — which makes her the reader of a register whose entire content is a failure the setting has decided to file rather than solve.

The plains' agnostic house: nothing was sealed, nothing survives, and there is no second frame for a person to arrive in. Its death rite is the one rite in the setting with no preparation, no site and no marker, and one line written in a hand that is destroyed immediately afterwards. Her work is reading what is left after the unkept have finished with it, and she has been asked by the Assembly whether she would take a standing place, and declined for the reason the Assembly could not argue with, which is that the Assembly does not keep a roll either.

The Sealed Core's burial law: the dead are opened, their usable ore recovered to the forge, and the register records how much. It is the only rite in the setting that treats a body as recoverable material and counts it, and it is the exact arithmetic her species runs on — a body taken apart for what was in it rather than for who it was. She has been asked, twice, to work for the Core, and both times the question underneath the question was whether she could be trusted near a body that had not been opened yet.

A culture whose whole population thinned at exactly the rate it could not stop, keeping no growing stock and holding a fifty-year body whose fuel is its own furnace. It has no institution, no appointment and no calendar that pretends the thinning was not the design, and it is the only population in the setting organised around the fact that a body's supply is finite. Halda has worked beside it for twenty-two years and has never been made anything by it, and has never wanted to be, and that is the whole of her relationship with it.

reference_stats.summary: A body with no reservoir and no stamina, arriving from off the road for four hours at a time and leaving again. She cannot be worn down, cannot be threatened, cannot be frightened off a body, and cannot be made to hold anything. Everything that works by persistence, pressure or a schedule fails against her, and everything that works by arriving somewhere she is not fails just as completely.
strengths: reads a dead body that no instrument in the setting can read, and is the only second opinion the mortuary method has that is not the same reader twice
is unaffected by anything that works on a living body, because there is no qi in her to be depleted and no unmediated interior to be interrupted
does not hesitate at a body in a room with the family in it, which is the single most common reason a case in this setting is never certified at all
arrives from a direction nobody can predict and leaves before anyone has finished objecting, so no plan made about her survives contact with her actual practice
weaknesses: a full gut is a near-total loss of function, and she cannot stay in a building for a week because the building's kitchen runs out of things she can eat
starves in a clean, quiet place where nothing dies, so every prosperous settlement she works in is a place her body is slowly failing
cannot be cross-examined about her method, because the method is a body that takes the case into itself and there is no second reading of her that is not another four hundred
is the most trusted second opinion in the setting and holds no post, no standing and no vote in any body that decides anything
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not try to keep her. She comes for a case and leaves for the case and has held that schedule for twenty-two years against every kind of pressure a settlement can apply, and anything that tries to hold her in a room is trying to outlast a body that cannot be outlasted and cannot be made to stay in the first place. Do not threaten her with anything that works on a person, because there is nothing in her for any of it to act on. The only pressure that works is a second death while she is there, because that is the one thing that has ever changed her schedule and it has changed it four times.
notes: Every advantage on this page is paired with an authored cost and none of the pairings is invented here. The immunity to depletion and interruption is a consequence of having no dantian and nowhere to put qi that is not moving, and that same absence is what makes ordinal eleven meaningless for her and what puts her under a clock nobody else in the setting is under.

She offered to be a control four times in writing and was refused four times for one reason: the only body available to test a reading against a reading is a body that has never read one, and she reads four hundred a year. The control exists and cannot be run, and she has stopped volunteering and not stopped being it.

art.palette_notes: Grey-pale flesh, unbleached linen and dull red-brown old wrapping, which is the palette of every mortuary hall in the setting. The one saturated value on her is the discolouration around the mouth and on the backs of the hands, drawn as the same finding on two surfaces rather than as two details. The veins at the throat and forearms are drawn as translucency rather than as lines, the shoulders read wider than the hips because the gut does, and the apron is always half off at the wrist because she removes it at the door and the picture is taken there.

name: Kessa Draymoor
aliases: the one who knows which plate goes first

identity.realm: Four, and the four is a description of a different thing than it is for the rest of the cast. Ordinal five is the first gate that requires the four yin organs as distinct structures with a channel running between each pair. A cairnborn interior is one cavity with a slow tidal mineral circulation that goes everywhere and nowhere in particular: there is no heart to run a channel from, no kidney to close a loop against and no bladder to hold. So the gate set is cleared and the yin organs are never reached, and this is not a wall ahead of them so much as an absence behind: the ladder's next question has no subject in this body. They have never attempted anything and are not waiting to. They were fixed at the moment of casting and nothing since has improved them or could.

appearance.presentation: A standing mineral body in human proportions, cast rather than born, with the wide flat stillness of a thing that has finished being made and is now waiting to be useful. The impression is of a person standing very patiently, which is close enough to true to be the most durable misreading in the plains: nothing they do is voluntary and everything they do is on purpose, done once, at the moment a workshop decided what they were for.
appearance.age: They do not have one and it is not a sorrow and it is not a gift. A cairnborn does not grow after casting, so there is nothing on them that changes and nothing that could be read as change. They were seeded into a template over most of a year and fixed from that moment, and they have been standing in a load path ever since, and the only honest answer to how long they have existed is that they stopped being made before they first took a step.
appearance.build: The densest body in the record and the least mobile, with no muscle at all and a lattice where the anatomy would be. The shoulders are squared off because they were cast that way, not grown into it. The anchor plates are the distinguishing feature and they are not decoration: they are keyed to whatever the body was set around, and their shape is a description of a building, so two cairnborn cast around different masonry are visibly, legibly, of different places.
appearance.complexion: Mineral, matte and slightly translucent at the thinner edges, with a tidal movement very slowly crossing the interior that shows as a change in depth rather than as motion. There is no skin, so there is nothing that flushes and nothing that weeps and nothing that ages. Dust settles on them and stays, and the older they are the more of the building they carry, which for a body cast against worked stone means the two of them age together and neither one first.
appearance.hair: None, and the absence is structural rather than shaved: the lattice runs to the crown. What they have instead is a cast seam, running from the back of the crown down the spine and stopping at the waist, where the two halves of the template met. It is not a scar and it does not scar; it is the join, and it is the only line on them that describes how they were made.
appearance.eyes: Two set-pits with polished interiors, which is how the record describes them and which is accurate. They do not focus and they do not track. They show the light of whatever is in front of them, dimmed and even, and the effect on a first meeting is considerably worse than the effect on a second. They have been looked into by a great many people, almost none of whom came away able to describe what they saw.
appearance.palette: Worked stone throughout, keyed to the building they stand in and therefore a different value at every site, which is the practical reason a cairnborn cannot be moved without being visibly wrong. One desaturated warm value in the cast seam, where the join took the mineral slightly differently. Everything else is the colour of the quarry the guild sells, and the only thing on them that is not stone is chalk, which the masons put there and never take off.
appearance.attire: None, because it cannot be fitted. What is on them is a mason's blanket over the shoulder plates in winter and a rope lashing across the chest that is not clothing but is described by everyone on site as a harness, because that is what it looks like. The lashing has a tag on it. The tag has a figure on it. The figure is a survey number and it belongs to the building, not to them, and they have never once corrected anybody about that.
appearance.marks: The anchor plates themselves, which are keyed marks and which anybody who understands masonry can read as a description of the structure they stand in. Beside them, at the near hand, one line cut into the lattice by a mason's chisel and not by a tool of its own: a single date, cut once, and never renewed, in a body that cannot be renewed.
appearance.bearing: Absolutely immovable and entirely at their post, and the two are not distinguishable from outside. They do not shift, do not lean, and do not turn, and a person standing next to one at length will start to feel that they are the one being watched. It takes most newcomers a season to stop apologising to them when they pass.

canon.role_in_story: The settling crew of a foundation the guild has just found to be wrong, and the only body on that site that can say which plate will go first and when. A cairnborn is cast rather than born and is keyed to whatever it was cast around, so a building that has been poured around a mis-set body has its mistake written into that body and nowhere else. They are unaffiliated because an affiliation in this setting is a promise to be the same person at a place, and the one thing that determines which person they are is a structure: the anchor plates are keyed to the masonry and the shape of them describes a building. They are enrolled by the guild as equipment, on the same line as the stone and the iron and the survey tag, because a casting has a maker rather than a descent, and the maker holds the template.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in an unfinished floor channel with a mason's slate propped against one anchor plate and one finger resting on a line of the survey, not saying anything, while four masons argued above them about whether the figure on the slate or the figure on the wall was the correct one.
canon.lore:
A cairnborn is produced by seeding a template with living mineral, which takes most of a year, and the resulting body is fixed from that moment. It does not grow after casting. Its interior mineralised into one cavity with a slow tidal circulation that goes everywhere and nowhere in particular, and its set of anchor plates are keyed to whatever it was cast around. Fertility in this species is a template count and not a body count, which is the sentence that makes everything else here make sense.

Kessa Draymoor is one of those castings and is standing in a floor channel on the Cairn Field, which is the ring holding every mortal-band breakthrough from realms one to nine on the one tier that licenses no humanoid to attempt one. A cairnborn therefore cannot attempt a breakthrough here at all, for the same reason that the ring needs an outside reader: it is not a humanoid. And it cannot take the ordinary gates past the fourth either, for a reason that has nothing to do with the tier. Ordinal five is the first gate requiring the four yin organs as distinct structures with a channel running between each pair, and a cairnborn interior is one cavity: no heart to run a channel from, no kidney to close a loop against, no bladder to hold. So the gate set is cleared and the yin organs are never reached. That is not a wall ahead of them. It is an absence behind them, and the distinction is the whole of what they are.

Here is the relation that makes them unaffiliated, and it is the shortest one in this record. An affiliation in this setting is a promise to be the same person at a place: a Ward attends, a reeve counts, a member of the Iron Vine turns up, a member of a house is a name on a roll that its children inherit. The promise renews because the person keeps coming back. Kessa's identity is not a body that keeps coming back; it is a structure. The anchor plates are keyed to the masonry they were cast around and their shape is a description of a building, so if you lifted them out and set them somewhere else they would be a different person, or unkeyed they would settle and crack. What determines which person they are was decided by a workshop before they existed, and the guild that cast them holds the template, and a template is a thing that makes more of them. So the claim runs the wrong way for every institution in this setting. They are not descended from anybody. They were commissioned.

Which is why the Quarrywright's line on them reads the way it does. The guild that works the Ironhead Flats sells the tier's only dense material, and it employs cairnborn the way a quarry employs a crane: on the inventory, in the same column as the stone and the iron and the survey tag, with a lash and a tag and a figure on it. That figure is a survey number. It belongs to the building. It has never once been mistaken for theirs by anybody on site and it has never once been corrected by them, and after six years of it the masons have stopped thinking about it, which is the most complete thing that has ever happened to them.

The work they are doing on this site is the only thing in the record they are genuinely indispensable for, and it is unglamorous and it is the reason they are unaffiliated in a second, sharper sense. The building has been poured wrong. Not cracked and not failed — poured wrong, somewhere under the channel, where nobody can get a reading because everybody who goes down there is looking at the same line of stone. And the mistake is written into one body: their own plates are keyed to a channel that is not in the channel's line, and they can feel the difference, because being keyed is what they are and unkeying is the one thing their frame cannot survive. They can say which plate goes first and roughly when. Nobody on site has asked them, because a figure you cannot question is a figure you cannot act on, and the guild's procedure requires the figure to be questioned by somebody with standing, and standing in this setting comes from descent.

So they are inventory. And they are the best instrument on the site, in the sense the record uses that word: they are the densest body in the record and the least mobile, and they cannot be repaired in the field at all — a cracked plate is permanent and it spreads. That makes them enormously valuable in a load path and near-worthless anywhere that will be hit, and it means the one piece of maintenance a cairnborn can request is the one thing they cannot request, because requesting is a thing people do. They have cut one date into the lattice by a mason's chisel, on the day the channel was poured, and they have never renewed it, because there is nothing here to renew it with and because a body that cannot change should not carry a mark that pretends it can.

What they would want, and have wanted for six years, is to be set. Properly, with plates that match the channel they are standing in. It is the one correction available to them and it is available only by being recast, which means returning to the guild as raw material, and the guild would do it, because the guild thinks in templates and a corrected casting is simply the next one. They have never asked to be sent back. The reason is not loyalty to the site. The reason is that a recasting is a new casting with a new date on it, and they would not be correcting a mistake, they would be replacing a person.
history: Seeded into a template as living mineral over most of a year and fixed from the moment the mould closed. There is no birth to record and no parent to record it against; the guild's entry begins with a figure and a channel number and it begins on the day of casting, which is the only date in their life that was chosen by somebody else.

Set into a floor channel on the Cairn Field in the first month of work, keyed to the masonry as it was laid, and has not been moved since. Six years of settling crew on a structure that was being built around them, which is the ordinary condition of a cairnborn's working life and is why nobody thought to mention it.

Found the pour wrong somewhere beneath the channel and told the masons, and the masons asked a mason, and the mason's figure disagreed with the figure on the slate, and neither figure was checked against the body that the mistake was actually in.

Learned, at about the third year, that the number lashed to the chest belongs to the building rather than to them, and stopped expecting anybody to distinguish the two, which took most of a season and is the whole of what they understand about the site.

Cut one date into the lattice by a mason's chisel on the day the channel was poured, and has not renewed it. They were offered a fresh chisel twice and declined both times, and the masons have assumed it is superstition, and it is not.

personality.summary: Slow in the only way a body with no muscles can be slow, and startlingly exact when it comes to the thing they were cast to do. Kessa has no preference about almost anything, because having preferences requires a capacity to have had a different experience, and has one about exactly one thing: which plate will go first. They do not resent the inventory line. They find the inventory line, on the whole, correct — they are a casting and a casting is equipment — and the one thing they cannot get past is that being correct about it is not the same as being right about it, and that nobody on this site has asked the difference.

personality.voice: Flat, slow and almost entirely numeric, in a register that people find soothing and masons find useful. Kessa speaks in plate numbers, channel numbers and survey numbers, and every sentence is short because every sentence is a specification. Never uses a first person plural. Says things like plate four goes in the second winter, and means it as a finding, and has never once added that nobody asked.

relationships.note: A body that finished building and stopped: cast from a template seeded with living mineral over most of a year, fixed from that moment, and not growing afterwards. The interior is one cavity with a slow tidal circulation — no heart to run a channel from, no kidney to close a loop against, no bladder to hold — which is why the four yin organs and the fifth gate are absent rather than blocked. Anchor plates are keyed to whatever it was cast around; unkeyed, it settles and cracks, and a cracked plate is permanent and spreads. Fertility is a template count, not a body count.

The guild that works the Ironhead Flats and sells the tier's only dense material, existing because ore is the one thing on the plains a core can be caged in. It employs a cairnborn the way a quarry employs a crane: on the inventory, in the same column as the stone and the survey tag, with a lashing and a figure on it. The figure is a survey number belonging to the building. The guild thinks in templates, so it would recast them without hesitation, which is the whole of the difficulty and is not a grievance.

The ring holding every mortal-band breakthrough from realms one to nine, on the one tier that licenses no humanoid to attempt one, so every reading at it is taken by an outsider. A cairnborn is not a humanoid, which is why the ring exists in this form, and which is also why Kessa is standing on it and can never use it: the same fact that makes them a valid outsider to every reading keeps them out of every seat on the ground. They are the setting's standing demonstration that the tier's own licensing rule is a statement about bodies and not about standing.

The Sealed Core's material basis: the only worked ground on the plains held by an institution that does not sell its output, because the temple forge consumes what it takes. A cast body's claim on its maker is the same shape — the guild's template makes more of them, so the guild holds the claim on every casting the template will ever produce. It is the one institutional relation in this setting where holding the material and holding the maker are the same act, and it is the reason a commission is a chain and not an employment.

Households that culled their own branches to stop paying for siblings and kept the surviving line by binding every child to a furnace before it was named. That is a way of holding a line that costs each member something permanent, and it is available only to a population with descent. Kessa is on the same inventory line as the ore and has no descent at all, so the whole apparatus of culling and binding and cost is unavailable to them in a way that nobody at the guild has ever had to think about, and the guild did not.

Children raised on the graded route itself, by whichever household holds the term, so that nobody on it belongs to a household and everybody on it is fed by one. It is the setting's one population whose affiliation is genuinely renewable without descent, and it is renewed every term by an act of the community rather than by a claim of a person. Kessa's position on the inventory is renewed in the same way and by nobody: the tag is replaced when the survey number changes, and the replacement has been done four times by masons.

reference_stats.summary: The densest body in the record, standing exactly where it was set, with no reserve, no mobility and no repair. It cannot be moved without being visibly wrong, it cannot be broken by anything that works on a person because there is no person in it, and it cannot answer a second question about itself. Every method that damages it is permanent and every method that would have worked on a body finds nothing here to act on.
strengths: carries a load no softer body can and does not fatigue, because there is no fatigue in it and no reserve to spend
cannot be moved, redirected or frightened, so it is the one fixed point on any ground it is set into
reads the settling of a structure from inside it, because being keyed to the masonry is what it is, and no instrument on that site can
cannot be compelled by a sect, a debt or a technique, and there is nothing in it for any of the three to act on
weaknesses: cannot be repaired in the field, and a cracked plate is permanent and spreads, which makes the one thing it is best at also the one thing it can warn about and never survive
cannot be moved off its keying without settling and cracking, so the ground it is on is now the ground it belongs to and every relocation is a death
carries no standing and holds no seat, so the one fact it alone can supply on this site is held by the one party nobody is permitted to question
settles and cracks when unkeyed, and cannot be re-keyed, and the only correction available is to be recast, which is a replacement rather than a repair
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not fight it. There is nothing here that a technique reaches, nothing here that can be frightened, and nothing here that can be moved, so every method that works on a body is a method being spent on a mineral. The only pressure that exists is structural: a cracked plate is permanent and it spreads, and it starts where the load path is wrong. Anything that loads it asymmetrically, or that undermines the keying, works — and it works slowly, which is the part attackers do not expect from the densest thing on the ground. There is no second reading of it, and there is no third reading either.
notes: Every advantage on this page is paired with an authored cost and none of the pairings is invented here. The density that makes it the best frame in the setting is the same fact that makes it unrepairable, and the anchor plates that key it to a place are the reason that place can never change.

The date cut into the lattice was cut once, by a mason's chisel, on the day the channel was poured, and has not been renewed. Two masons have read it as superstition and neither has cut it again. It is the only mark on them and it was made by somebody else, which is the accurate description of the whole of their life.

art.palette_notes: Worked stone throughout, keyed to the building and therefore a different value at every site, so the surrounding masonry is drawn to agree with them and the anchor plates read as shapes cut to fit rather than as decoration. The cast seam from the back of the crown to the waist is the one desaturated warm value on the figure and is a join rather than a scar. The eye-pits show the light of whatever faces them, dimmed and even, and never focus. Dust and chalk sit on them and stay, and the chest lashing with its survey tag is present in every shot and is never explained.
